# Email Validation Function

Here's a short JavaScript function that validates basic well-formed email addresses using a regular expression:

```javascript
function isValidEmail(email) {
  return /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email);
}
```

## How the Regex Works

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| `^` | Start of string |
| `[^\s@]+` | One or more chars that aren't whitespace or `@` (local part) |
| `@` | Literal `@` symbol |
| `[^\s@]+` | One or more chars that aren't whitespace or `@` (domain) |
| `\.` | Literal dot |
| `[^\s@]+` | One or more chars (TLD) |
| `$` | End of string |

## Examples

```javascript
console.log(isValidEmail("user@example.com"));    // true
console.log(isValidEmail("john.doe@mail.co.uk"));  // true
console.log(isValidEmail("invalid@"));             // false
console.log(isValidEmail("no-at-sign.com"));       // false
console.log(isValidEmail("user@domain"));          // false (no TLD)
console.log(isValidEmail("has space@x.com"));      // false
```

> **Note:** This is a *basic* validator suitable for catching obvious mistakes. Fully RFC 5322-compliant email validation is far more complex, so for critical use cases, consider sending a verification email instead.
